newsitem.title: USA: Cleveland-Cliffs says sales above 1996 Y2.
newsitem.headline: Cleveland-Cliffs says sales above 1996 Y2.

text.p: Cleveland-Cliffs Inc said on Tuesday that despite a slowdown in sales in the first half of the year, it expected sales for the balance of the year modestly to exceed last year's second-half levels.
In addition, the company predicted sales for the full year would come in at roughly 10.4 million tons.
"While first-half sales were slower than normal, sales for the balance of the year are expected to modestly exceed last year's second-half," said chief executive, M. Thomas Moore.

He continued: "Average pellet prices have been essentially even with last year. However, mine operating performance has been unfavorable. Extensive efforts to overcome operating difficulties are expected to improve second-half performance."
Cleveland-Cliffs, a supplier of iron ore products to the steel industry, posted second quarter earnings of $1.14 per share, compared with $1.52 for the year-ago period.
